newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macmin says Simuku results encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Macmin says Simuku results encouraging.

text.p: Junior miner Macmin NL said on Thursday a drilling and trenching programme at its 45 percent owned Simuku project in Papua New Guinea has defined a large zone of porphyry copper and gold mineralisation.
Macmin said the zone extends over an area of four to five square kilometres, and is open ended to the north and south.
Best results included 36 metres at 0.7 percent copper with 0.1 grams per tonne of gold from 30 metres, and 77 metres at 0.5 percent copper with 0.11 grams per tonne of gold over the entire hole.
"Drilling results were very encouraging with copper, gold and molybdenum mineralisation intersected in most holes," Macmin said in a statement.
Continuing exploration at the project, on the island of New Britain, was designed to locate higher grade zones.
Macmin's partner, New Guinea Gold Corp of Canada, is earning a 55 percent interest in Simuku through exploration funding.
